title: Personalized Matchday: What a Smarter Royal Challengers Bengaluru App Could Offer
dek: A smarter Royal Challengers Bengaluru app would know what a fan cares about and when to interrupt them. The match data shows how many moments a typical game offers to personalise.
excerpt: A typical Royal Challengers Bengaluru match since 2024 has produced dozens of boundaries, a dozen or so wickets and at least one fifty. A personalised app would choose which of those each fan hears about.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: Across {{ev:pm-n}} RCB matches since 2024, each produced {{ev:pm-four}} fours, {{ev:pm-six}} sixes and {{ev:pm-wk}} wickets on average.
There were {{ev:pm-fif}} fifties per match, and {{ev:pm-close}} of decided matches were close finishes.
A personalised app would filter those moments by player, phase and match situation.

sections.heading: Too Many Moments to Notify
body: A generic app alerts every fan to every wicket. A personalised one would know who you follow and what matters to you.

Across {{ev:pm-n}} Royal Challengers Bengaluru matches since 2024, each produced {{ev:pm-four}} fours, {{ev:pm-six}} sixes and {{ev:pm-wk}} wickets on average, both sides combined, with {{ev:pm-fif}} fifties per match.

sections.heading: When to Interrupt
body: {{ev:pm-close}} of decided RCB matches since 2024 were close finishes: the matches where a "come back now" alert is worth sending.
The win-probability model in this series could trigger that alert when a match tightens.

sections.heading: Proposal: A Smarter App
body: Proposal: player-follow alerts for milestones, a tension alert driven by win probability, and an end-of-match card built from each fan's followed players.

sections.heading: Privacy First
body: Personalisation needs data about fans. Any such app should collect the minimum, explain it clearly and let fans opt out, in line with the data-governance article in this series.
The match data itself is public; fan data is not.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Personalise the Moments, Not the Fan
body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru can build most of a smarter matchday app from match data alone, with fans choosing what they follow.
That respects privacy while still cutting the noise.
